newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Rubber - SE Asian market weak despite inquiries.
newsitem.headline: Rubber - SE Asian market weak despite inquiries.

text.p: Southeast Asian rubber prices will probably remain soft this week due to high stocks in Japan and weak demand from the United States, traders said on Monday.
Fresh buying inquiries in Malaysia and Indonesia may help shore up prices there, but the overall mood of the market remains shaky, they said.
"I think the basic trend is still bearish," a trader at a Western commodity house in Singapore said. "We need to see much better demand from the United States than we've seen so far."
A slightly tighter supply situation was offset by high rubber stocks in Japan, which is bad news for the market, dealers said.
"A smaller supply could support the price, but I don't expect to see any rally if demand continues to be sluggish," said a Thai trader.

Another dealer said a rally in Japanese futures markets last week, which briefly pushed the price of Tokyo's benchmark March contract to an intra-week high of 136 yen a kg on Friday, was quickly shorted out by profit-taking, further depressing rubber prices on the Singapore Commodities Exchange.
"We'll see how Japan performs this week, but the whole market is depressed because demand is so weak," he said.
Thai rubber prices were barely changed last week despite light buying by Chinese and Japanese consumers, traders said.
The Thai benchmark RSS3 for November shipment was quoted at around US$1.23-1.25 a kg FOB Bangkok on Friday against $1.24-1.26 the previous week.
Thai latex was quoted at 93-95 cents a kg on Friday.
"There were some Chinese and Japanese buyers in the market, but they only purchased small amounts," one Thai trader said.
"I think demand in China remains good. However, some were cautious about their (Chinese buyers') credit and were reluctant to sell much," he added.

Rains in southern Thailand hindered rubber tapping, resulting in lower supplies. Only 330,877 kgs of rubber was traded in the local market last week, compared with the previous week's 626,437 kgs, traders said.
In Indonesia, benchmark SIR20 rubber prices are likely to trend steady this week as prices are considered to have hit rock bottom after several weeks of poor demand, dealers said.
"We have started to receive a higher number of fresh inquiries in the past several days. We expect more deals to come," one dealer in Jakarta said.
One Medan-based dealer, however, said that offtake and any possible price rises, were likely to be limited by underlying lacklustre demand.

Dealers said SIR20 offer prices for November were expected to be steady at 55.25-55.50 U.S. cents/lb fob Medan and at 54.50-55.25 cents fob Palembang, Surabaya and Padang, and at 54.50-55.00 cents fob Jambi and Pontianak.
SIR10 was also seen trending steadily following recent deals with U.S. firms buying at 120.5 cents/kg fob Medan for November delivery, another Jakarta-based dealer said.

Dealers said supply was not as tight as had been expected as the rains mostly fell during the afternoon and evenings which generally does not have much impact on tapping as this is concentrated in the morning when latex flow is highest.

High ammoniac grade latex with 60 percent dry rubber content is expected to be on offer at between 2,275-2,485 rupiah/kg this week against the previous 2,250 rupiah in the local markets of Bandung and Tangerang, they said.
Malaysian dealers said more rainfall this week could help support the market's downside and even allow slight gains if the supply of latex and stocks come under pressure.
Benchmark RSS1 closed at Malaysian 310.50 cents a kg on Friday while SMR20 was quoted at 306.00 cents.
"I think RSS1 could touch between 313-315 and (SMR)20 305-308," a dealer with a foreign rubber trading house said. "But this will still depend on demand."

Buying interest in Malaysia has been weak in the last fortnight, with U.S. and European buyers noticeably missing, traders said. Chinese and Middle East consumers, meanwhile, have only been present to check the daily trade for prices or to engage in some short-covering, dealers said.
"The heavy rain for the last two weeks has kept prices from getting too soft. But latex has been affected more than other raw materials," said another dealer.
He said supply of drum latex was "quite comfortable" and was the main reason why prices of the material fell faster.
On Friday, latex was being offered by trading houses at around 234 to 235 cents a kg.
(With contributions from Jakarta, Bangkok and Kuala Lumpur)
- Singapore Newsroom (65-8703305)
